title: DNA Extraction Protocol for Low-Biomass Environmental Samples
author: Jiaxian Shen
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.21203/rs.3.pex-1658/v1
materials: (Thoroughly mix the various Lysis Solutions to ensure uniform composition before dispensing.) Dilute 1.666 µL of Proteinase K into 250 µL of 2X T and C Lysis Solution for each sample.

steps.title: Set equipment temperatures
steps.instruction: Set the ThermoMixer to 65 °C and the centrifuge to 4 °C.

steps.title: Add sample and lysis buffer
steps.instruction: Transfer 250 µL fluid sample to an O‑ring tube prefilled with beads, add 250 µL 2X T and C Lysis Solution containing Proteinase K, and vortex thoroughly.

steps.title: Bead‑beating lysis
steps.instruction: Bead‑beat for 5 minutes, processing no more than 12 tubes at a time.

steps.title: Incubate lysate at 65 °C
steps.instruction: Incubate in the ThermoMixer at 65 °C for 25 minutes, vortex every 5 minutes, and maintain shaking speed at 300 rpm.

steps.title: Centrifuge to clarify
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tubes at 12,000 × g for 3 minutes at room temperature.

steps.title: Transfer first supernatant
steps.instruction: Using a 1000 µL pipette followed by a 20 µL pipette, transfer 350 µL + 10 µL supernatant to a new microcentrifuge tube; this volume was determined experimentally and may be adjusted and documented for different samples.

steps.title: Cool and add RNase A
steps.instruction: Change the ThermoMixer temperature to 37 °C and wait until it reaches 37 °C, then add 1.666 µL of 5 mg/mL RNase A and mix thoroughly.

steps.title: RNase digestion
steps.instruction: Incubate at 37 °C for 50 minutes while shaking at 300 rpm.

steps.title: Ice chill before precipitation
steps.instruction: Place the samples on ice for 5–8 minutes.

steps.title: Add MPC precipitation reagent
steps.instruction: Add 330 µL MPC Protein Precipitation Reagent to the lysed sample and vortex vigorously for 10 seconds.

steps.title: Pellet debris
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 4 °C, 16,000 × g for 18 minutes. If the resultant pellet is clear, small, or loose, add an additional 25 µL MPC Protein Precipitation Reagent, mix, and repeat centrifugation. Note: this protocol adds 80 µL more MPC reagent than the kit manual.

steps.title: Transfer cleared supernatant
steps.instruction: Transfer the supernatant to a clean microcentrifuge tube, discarding the pellet; use a 1000 µL pipette followed by a 20 µL pipette gently to recover the maximum possible volume while keeping the pellet intact. Expected ~670 µL, observed ~600 µL + 20 µL; document the actual volume.

steps.title: Precipitate DNA with isopropanol
steps.instruction: Add 834 µL isopropanol to the recovered supernatant and invert the tube 50–60 times.

steps.title: Remove isopropanol
steps.instruction: Carefully remove the isopropanol with a pipette without dislodging the DNA pellet.

steps.title: Ethanol wash DNA
steps.instruction: Rinse the pellet twice with fresh 70 % ethanol, avoiding dislodgement; centrifuge briefly between washes (2 minutes at 16,000 × g) and remove all residual ethanol with a pipette.

steps.title: Vacuum‑dry DNA pellet
steps.instruction: Vacuum‑centrifuge the sample at room temperature for 2 minutes under V‑AQ mode (DNA pellet turns from white to transparent). Optionally add 1 minute (or 30 seconds) extra drying time for new samples; reference: 2 minutes + 1 minute used.

steps.title: Resuspend DNA
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL DNase‑free water, gently flick the tube to disrupt the pellet, and if necessary leave at 4 °C overnight to rehydrate.
